title: Dal Tadka

items: 1/2 cup masoor dal / dehusked brown lentils
1/4 cup moong dal / skinned, split green gram
1/4 cup tuvar / arhar dal / pigeon pea lentils
10-15 garlic cloves, ground to paste (~ 1:1 with ginger by volume, but heavier on garlic)
(replace ginger and garlic above with 3 one-inch cubes of ginger garlic paste.)
1 tsp kasuri methi (fenugreek leaves, not seeds), crushed

steps: Rinse the dal (lentil) until the water runs clear, then transfer to a pressure cooker and soak in 3 cups of fresh water for 10-15 minutes.
Add turmeric and salt, then pressure cook on high in the instant pot for 5 minutes then let it naturally release pressure (15-20 minutes).
Meanwhile, heat oil and ghee over medium-high heat.
Bloom the cumin seeds , asafotida, and chili pods in the oil until you start to hear crackles, about 15-30 seconds.
Add curry leaves, chopped onion, ginger paste, garlic paste, chopped tomato, chopped green chilis, dash of turmeric, chili powder, coriander powder, crushed fenugreek.
Saute for around 2 minutes over medium heat.
Reserve a portion of the mixture for garnish then add the cooked dal to the pot, stirring to combine.
Adjust salt to taste, then simmer for 1 minute until slightly thickened.
Add cilantro and butter then remove from heat, stirring until the butter is melted.  Serve immediately with a side of rice or naan, drizzling a spoon of the reserved mixture over top as garnish.
reviewFlags: The source lists 5 cups water but directs soaking in 3 cups, and the method calls for green chilis without an amount.
